thread:
maya singh: quick check — after the handoff RFC, i want to sync on the exact "safety surfaces" we own vs what the edge/runtime should assume. i kept encountering fuzzy cases during the sim runs. can we list the caller-facing invariants we need to preserve for active-active handoffs?
kevin wu: agree. what do you mean by safety surface exactly? e.g., allowed to drop KV cache entries? allowed to take short read-only mode?
anika patel: from product/legal: we also need to make sure residency hints are honored during handoff. if a tenant is resident in eu-west, we can’t silently switch to us-east for writes. that constraint changes the tradeoffs.
maya singh: by safety surface i mean the explicit guarantees we expose to callers and runbooks: 1) write-finality (accept or reject), 2) residency-respect (block or explicit consent), 3) max-dual-write-window (how long two primaries might both accept writes), 4) in-flight-request fate (retry vs fail).
devon r.: practical impl note: we can reduce dual-write window by making handoff require a lease_version handshake. if old-primary refuses to handoff until it drains outstanding requests -> longer incidence of unavailability.
kevin wu: proposal: expose a three-level fallback policy on the routing layer: "local-strict" (reject if not resident), "local-preferred" (try local, fallback with consent header), "any-region" (blind fallback). callers choose at route time.
maya singh: +1. i want to add a small header that the runtime can use for safe handoff decisions: Handoff-Intent: {consent:true|false, desired_consistency:final|eventual, max_staleness_ms:NNN} 
lia (platform): is that part of the public API or internal rpc metadata? we should keep public surface minimal; prefer internal per-tenant routing metadata and a thin public hint that maps to policy templates.
anika patel: legal says public hint is fine as long as default is conservative (local-strict) and we document fallback behaviors and consent logging.
kevin wu: implementation sketch for internal RPC header (runtime->proxy):
```
Handoff-Intent: consent=true;consistency=final;lease_version=2026-03-01T12:34:56Z;max_staleness_ms=50
```
runtime will: if consent=false && tenant_resident && not owner -> return 409 + residency_hint. if consent=true -> attempt cross-region forward with a routing ticket that includes lease_version.
sre-bot: simulation job queued: handoff-sim/3789019999 started (50k synthetic tenants, 10% cross-region write). logs -> https://ci.example/redwood/handoff-sim/3789019999
devon r.: one big risk: kv-cache ownership split during partial network partition. we should define safe eviction semantics: owner can mark epoch as quarantined and forward a tombstone to proxies. proxies should honor tombstones for N seconds before accepting new writes locally. this avoids split-brain.
maya singh: yes — propose quarantine TTL metricized and automatic rollbacks if lease_version mismatch observed. also add a health-check gate: if routing observes >X% 409s, trigger a canary rollback and alert.
lia (platform): rollout plan: 1) add header support and server-side shadow path (no behavioral change), 2) run sims + perf tests, 3) enable for subset of tenants under a feature flag, 4) 2-week observation, 5) full on. add cost telemetry (extra cross-region tokens) to avoid surprises.
anika patel: add an audit log entry whenever fallback consent=true is used (for compliance). also keep a per-tenant residency override config.
kevin wu: action items: - maya to open follow-up RFC with the exact header schema and operator runbook (owner: maya) - devon to prototype tombstone/quarantine signals in sim infra - lia to add metrics set + alerts - anika to draft compliance blurb for docs
maya singh: i'll open RFC today and include the sim results that motivated this. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
